- [Proposed U.S. takeover of the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Donald_Trump_Gaza_Strip_takeover_proposal "2025 Donald Trump Gaza Strip takeover proposal") | On 7 October 2023, [a large escalation of the Gaza–Israel conflict began](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") with a [coordinated offensive by multiple Palestinian militant groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks"), led by [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas"), against [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"). A number of countries, including many of Israel's Western allies, such as the United States and a number of European countries, condemned the attacks led by Hamas, expressed solidarity for Israel and stated that Israel has a right to defend itself from armed attacks, while countries in the [Islamic world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_world "Islamic world") (including the [Axis of Resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance "Axis of Resistance")) expressed support for the Palestinians, blaming the [Israeli occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation "Israeli occupation") of the [Palestinian territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories "Palestinian territories") as being the root cause for the escalation of violence. The events prompted several world leaders to announce their intention to visit Israel, including US President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"),[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-4) French President [Emmanuel Macron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Macron "Emmanuel Macron"),[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-7) German Chancellor [Olaf Scholz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_Scholz "Olaf Scholz"),[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-independent-diplomaticties-11) and British Prime Minister [Rishi Sunak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishi_Sunak "Rishi Sunak").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-14) Numerous countries [called for a ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calls_for_a_ceasefire_during_the_Gaza_war "Calls for a ceasefire during the Gaza war") and de-escalation. International organizations, student organizations, charities, ecumenical Christian organizations, and Jewish and Islamic groups commented on the situation. On 27 October 2023, the [United Nations General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly") passed [a resolution calling Israel (Genocide Convention)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa's_genocide_case_against_Israel "South Africa's genocide case against Israel")_ to the [International Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice"), arguing that Israel was responsible for [a genocide of Palestinians in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide").[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-65) In May 2024, ICJ judges called on Israel to halt its intended [military offensive in the city of Rafah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafah_offensive "Rafah offensive").[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-66) - The bill now awaits consideration by the US Senate.[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-128)[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-129) On 8 February, Biden called Israel's actions in Gaza "over the top".[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-130) Following this, the Biden administration issued a [national security directive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security_directive "National security directive") requiring written assurances from Israel (and other countries) that it was using US-supplied weapons in line with international law.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-131)[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-132) On 20 February, the US proposed a draft UN Security Council resolution, calling for a "temporary ceasefire in Gaza as soon as practicable, based on the formula of all hostages being released". ![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Flag_of_Australia_%28converted%29.svg/40px-Flag_of_Australia_%28converted%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"): Foreign Minister [Penny Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Wong "Penny Wong") said that "Australia unequivocally condemns the attacks on Israel by Hamas including indiscriminate rocket fire on cities and civilians."[\[382\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-382) [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia "Prime Minister of Australia") [Anthony Albanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Albanese "Anthony Albanese") also strongly condemned the attacks.[\[383\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-383) In July 2025, Australia and several other Western countries issued a joint statement calling for an immediate end to the war in Gaza.[\[279\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:28-279) - Hipkins also stated Israel had the right to defend itself.[\[398\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-398) On 25 October Carolyn Schwalger, New Zealand's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, delivered a statement to the [United Nations Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") calling for a "humanitarian pause" to allow Gazan civilians to receive aid and for the creation of safe zones.[\[399\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-399) By 18 November, New Zealand had contributed a total of NZ$10 million to support humanitarian activities by the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") and [World Food Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Food_Programme "World Food Programme") in Israel and the Palestinian Territories.[\[400\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-400) - He also called on Hamas and other militant groups to resolve matters in relation to Israel through dialogue and called on Israel to consider its response to the attacks.[\[402\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-402) In June 2025, Papua New Guinea voted against a resolution calling for a ceasefire at the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations").[\[395\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:29-395) - ![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Flag_of_Europe.svg/40px-Flag_of_Europe.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"): President of the European Commission [Ursula von der Leyen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursula_von_der_Leyen "Ursula von der Leyen") said she "unequivocally" condemned "the attack carried out by Hamas terrorists against Israel", calling it "terrorism in its most despicable form" and saying "Israel has the right to defend itself against such heinous attacks".[\[406\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-406)[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:4-112) EU ambassador to Israel [Dimiter Tzantchev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimiter_Tzantchev "Dimiter Tzantchev") condemned the attack.[\[407\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-407) Israeli flags were raised outside the headquarters of the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") and the [European Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), while the latter's president [Roberta Metsola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_Metsola "Roberta Metsola") led a vigil in the chamber on 11 October to commemorate the Israeli victims of the attack which also featured a minute's silence and a rendition of the [Israeli national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatikvah "Hatikvah"). On 9 October, ahead of the EU council meeting convened to define a common EU position, EU Enlargement Commissioner [Oliver Varhelyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Varhelyi "Oliver Varhelyi") announced on X that the European Commission would be suspending immediately all payments due in developmental aid to Palestine.[\[408\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-408) The consensus emanating from the 9 October ministers meeting was a resolution condemning attacks by Hamas but also calling "for the protection of civilians and restraint, the release of hostages, for allowing access to food, water and medicines to Gaza in line with international humanitarian law".[\[409\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-409) The announcement by Varhelyi was criticized by the foreign ministers of several EU members state such as Spain, Ireland, Belgium and Luxembourg who insisted that only individual countries could make such decisions. The bloc corrected Varhelyi's announcement and said that it would review payments instead to prevent misuse.[\[257\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-landmark-257) In the [United Nations General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly") vote on [the resolution calling for](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_Resolution_ES-10/21 "United Nations General Assembly Resolution ES-10/21") an immediate and sustained humanitarian truce and cessation of hostilities, eight EU states voted in favour, four against and 15 abstained.[\[410\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-ap-20231028-410) Ursula von der Leyen and other European leaders were reluctant to impose [sanctions on Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott,_Divestment_and_Sanctions "Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions") despite clear violations of international law.[\[411\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-411) On 26 January 2024, the EU Commission and the High Representative issued a joint communication endorsing the International Court of Justice's order on South Africa's request for the indication of provisional measures in regard of the [Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. The IOC also stated that athletes are not to be held accountable for their government's actions.[\[636\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-636) Due to the continuation of the Israeli-Palestinian war, France asked the United States for help in securing the Olympic Games.[\[637\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-637) In March 2024, IOC President [Thomas Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bach "Thomas Bach") made it clear there was no issue regarding Israel participating at the 2024 Summer Olympics and cautioned athletes against boycotts and discrimination.[\[638\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-638) On 8 October 2023, [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") cancelled all of its scheduled football matches in Israel for the next two weeks, including a qualifier for the [Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_2024 "Euro 2024") tournament between [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_national_football_team "Israel national football team") and [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team "Switzerland national football team") on 12 October. It also canceled the [2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_European_Under-21_Championship_qualification "2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification") games between Israel and [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia_national_football_team "Estonia national football team") on 12 October and between Israel and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") on 17 October, as well as the [2024 UEFA European Under-17 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_European_Under-17_Championship "2024 UEFA European Under-17 Championship") mini tournament on 11–17 October involving Israel, [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team"), [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar_national_football_team "Gibraltar national football team") and [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales_national_football_team "Wales national football team").[\[639\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-639) UEFA held a moment of silence for all Euro 2024 qualifying matches on 17 October for both the victims of the war in Israel as well as the [Swedish fans that were murdered in Brussels a day prior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Brussels_shooting "2023 Brussels shooting"). Israel later played the rest of their Euro 2024 qualification matches in [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary "Hungary"), while [Maccabi Haifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Haifa_F.C. "Maccabi Haifa F.C.") played a Europa League match in [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus") before heading to [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") alongside [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_F.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C."). [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague") Basketball also suspended all home games for Israeli clubs, including [Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.") and [Maccabi Playtika Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Playtika_Tel_Aviv "Maccabi Playtika Tel Aviv"), with the teams sending its players to [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus") and [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") to possibly resume the season there. All EuroLeague and EuroCup matches held a moment of silence for the victims of the attack.[\[640\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-640)[\[641\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-641) The [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League"), [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association"), [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball"), [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League"), and [Major League Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Soccer "Major League Soccer"), amongst several other North American leagues, all released statements condemning the terrorist attacks on Israeli civilians by Hamas while urging for peace for civilians in the region. Many teams in their respective leagues also released their own statements with the same message. However, there was criticism towards all the leagues and teams for not releasing statements for the Palestinian civilians that had also been killed in the conflict.[\[642\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-642)[\[643\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-643)[\[644\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-644) All NFL teams during Week 6 held a moment of silence for the Israeli and American victims as well as those affected by the conflict, starting with a Thursday Night game between the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") and [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs").[\[645\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-645) However, during the London game between the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") and [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), the moment of silence was interrupted by some spectators chanting "Free Palestine". In the United Kingdom, there was pressure for the [English FA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") and the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") to release statements and honour the victims of the attacks by Hamas, with some noting that other tragedies, disasters, and social movements had been honoured much more quickly.[\[646\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-646)[\[647\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-647) Eventually the English FA honoured both the Israeli and Palestinian victims at a friendly with [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_men's_national_soccer_team "Australia men's national soccer team") and a [UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024_qualifying_Group_C "UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group C") with [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). However, they did not light up [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in the colours of the Israeli flag, believed to be due to one of Australia's 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifier opponents being [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_national_football_team "Palestine national football team").[\[648\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-648)[\[649\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-649) The Premier League also honoured the victims following the international break.[\[650\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-650) The FA has also banned the use of the phrase " [from the river to the sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/From_the_river_to_the_sea "From the river to the sea")" on any players' social media following its use by [Hamza Choudhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamza_Choudhury "Hamza Choudhury").[\[651\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-651) Following a request from the [Palestinian Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Football_Association "Palestinian Football Association")'s head [Jibril Rajoub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jibril_Rajoub "Jibril Rajoub"), the [Algerian Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_Football_Federation "Algerian Football Federation") offered to host "all official and non-official matches" of the Palestinian national team as part of its preparations for its qualifiers for the [2026 World Cup and 2027 Asian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_AFC_second_round "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – AFC second round"). It also pledged to shoulder all associated costs.[\[652\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-652) The PFA later accepted Algeria's request, though after FIFA and the AFC prevented the team from playing in Algeria, they selected [Kuwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait "Kuwait"), [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), and other countries in the [Islamic world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_world "Islamic world") instead. [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon_national_football_team "Lebanon national football team"), Palestine and Israel's neighbour to the north, were also forced to play the same 2026 World Cup and 2027 Asian Cup qualification in neutral ground due to the fear of the war's spillover to the country.[\[653\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-653) [Celtic F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C.") was fined 17,500 euros ($19,000) by UEFA after fans displayed a flag of the [Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_Front_for_the_Liberation_of_Palestine "Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine") during a [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") match against [Atletico Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atletico_Madrid "Atletico Madrid") on 25 October.[\[654\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-654) A number of people protested at the Paris Organizing Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games headquarters in the suburb of [Saint-Denis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Denis,_Seine-Saint-Denis "Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis"), waving Palestinian flags and chanting slogans condemning Israel's "institutional involvement" in the Games as a result of the ongoing conflict in Gaza. The demonstrators urged Olympic authorities to restrict Israel's involvement in the Paris Games.[\[655\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-655) The left-wing [Podemos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Podemos_(Spanish_political_party) "Podemos (Spanish political party)") party in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") requested the exclusion of Israel from the Olympics and called on countries to boycott the competition if Israeli continued to participate.[\[656\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-656)[\[657\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-657) Ione Belarra, the Podemos party's secretary general and former minister of social rights in Spain, called for Israel to be removed from the Olympics.[\[658\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-658) During the 74th [FIFA Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Congress "FIFA Congress") on 17 May 2024 in [Bangkok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangkok "Bangkok"), the [Palestinian Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Football_Association "Palestinian Football Association") called for a vote on suspending the IFA from both UEFA and FIFA, stating that the damage to football infrastructure and deaths of Palestinian footballers during the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") were enough grounds to justify the action, while other supporters referred to other suspensions such as those of [Apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid") [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa") from 1961 to 1991 and [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") following the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine") in 2022. The IFA responded stating that their football was halted and that many of their footballers have been killed since [7 October 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hamas-led_attack_on_Israel "2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel") while calling for peace and a future friendly between the two countries. [Gianni Infantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Infantino "Gianni Infantino") would respond to the PFA stating that FIFA would conduct its own legal review and that the information about a final decision would be forwarded to the FIFA Council meeting on 3 October 2024 while also calling for peace.[\[659\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-659)[\[660\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-660) It was later decided that while Israel would not be suspended, FIFA would investigate the claims by the PFA.[\[661\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-661) Prior to [qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2026 FIFA World Cup qualification") for the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup"), the [Norwegian Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Football_Federation "Norwegian Football Federation") called for an investigation into Israel (who they were drawn against), stating that they wanted to end civilian casualties in the region.[\[662\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-662) ### Individual athletes [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayern_Munich "Bayern Munich") and [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team "Morocco national football team") defender [Noussair Mazraoui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noussair_Mazraoui "Noussair Mazraoui") posted in support of Palestine on social media.[\[663\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-663) [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.") ended its contract with Israeli player [Eden Karzev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Karzev "Eden Karzev") after he re-posted a social media message with the hashtag "BringThemHomeNow", referring to the hostages held by Hamas.[\[679\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-679) ## Other organizations [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Yuval_Raphael_at_ESC2025_for_Israel_3.jpg/250px-Yuval_Raphael_at_ESC2025_for_Israel_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yuval_Raphael_at_ESC2025_for_Israel_3.jpg) Pro-Palestinian protest during the opening ceremony of the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025 "Eurovision Song Contest 2025") in [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel "Basel"), Switzerland, 11 May 2025 On 16 February 2024 a coalition of several U.S. unions announced a call for a ceasefire. The unions claim to represent some nine million teachers, nurses, auto workers,[\[680\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-680) flight attendants and others.[\[681\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-681) ### Eurovision Song Contest 2024 The [ongoing humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "2023 Gaza humanitarian crisis") resulting from the Israeli retaliatory operations in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 led to increasing calls that the [European Broadcasting Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Broadcasting_Union "European Broadcasting Union") (EBU) exclude Israel from taking part in the [Eurovision Song Contest 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2024 "Eurovision Song Contest 2024"), with human rights activists urging other countries to boycott the event.[\[682\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-682) Despite this, Israel ultimately appeared on the list of participants released by the EBU on 5 December 2023.[\[683\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-683)[\[684\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-684) The EBU said in a statement: "It is a competition for broadcasters (not governments) and the [Israeli public broadcaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Public_Broadcasting_Corporation "Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation") has participated in the Contest for 50 years. The Eurovision Song Contest remains a non-political event that unites audiences worldwide through music."[\[685\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-685) The Icelandic Association of Composers and Lyricists (FTT), which represents artists in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland"), told its members in a statement to not participate in the [Eurovision Song Contest 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2024 "Israel in the Eurovision Song Contest 2024") unless Israel is removed from the competition, on the same grounds as [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") was in the last competition, due to Israel's conduct in the Gaza war.[\[686\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-686) FTT also urged the [Icelandic National Broadcaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%9AV "RÚV") (RÚV) to withdraw from the competition unless Israel is denied participation on the same grounds as Russia was due to its [invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine").[\[687\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-687) ### Transatlantic Civil Servants' Statement on Gaza The Transatlantic Civil Servants' Statement on Gaza is a public letter signed by over 800 currently serving officials in the United States and Europe which states that the policies of their governments during the [Israel-Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel-Gaza_war "Israel-Gaza war") could amount to "grave violations of international law". The signatories are civil servants from the United States, the European Union, and 11 European countries including France, Germany, and the United Kingdom. Opinion polling ### Europe In Britain, a [YouGov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouGov "YouGov") poll conducted on 19 October found that 76% of respondents supported a ceasefire in the Gaza war.[\[801\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-801) An [Ipsos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipsos "Ipsos") poll carried out on 20–23 October, found that 37% of British respondents wanted the UK government to be a neutral mediator in the conflict, 16% wanted Britain to stay out of the conflict at all, 13% would support Israel and 12% would support Palestine.[\[802\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-802) According to a YouGov poll conducted on 7–8 November 2023, older people and [Conservatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") are more likely to sympathize with the Israelis, while younger people and [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_(UK) "Labour Party (UK)") voters are more likely to sympathize with the Palestinians.[\[803\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-803) According to a poll conducted by the [Forsa Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forsa_Institute "Forsa Institute") on behalf of newspaper _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Welt "Die Welt")_ in December 2023, 45% of respondents in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") agreed and 43% disagreed with the statement "Israel's military action in the Gaza Strip is all in all appropriate". In the immediate aftermath of the Hamas attack on Israel, 44% of Germans said Germany has "a special obligation towards Israel". In December 2023, that number dropped to 37%.[\[804\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-804) A survey commissioned by [Baltic News Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_News_Service "Baltic News Service") in November found that 38.1% of respondents in [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania") supported Israel's actions in Gaza, 30.4% did not support and 31.5% had no opinion.[\[805\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-805) Voters of the [Homeland Union-Lithuanian Christian Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeland_Union-Lithuanian_Christian_Democrats "Homeland Union-Lithuanian Christian Democrats") (58.8%), [Union of Democrats "For Lithuania"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_Democrats_%22For_Lithuania%22 "Union of Democrats \"For Lithuania\""), [Liberals' Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberals'_Movement_(Lithuania) "Liberals' Movement (Lithuania)") and [Freedom Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_Party_(Lithuania) "Freedom Party (Lithuania)") were most in favor of Israel's actions, while voters of [Lithuanian Regions Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_Regions_Party "Lithuanian Regions Party") and [People and Justice Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_and_Justice_Union "People and Justice Union") were least in favor.[\[806\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-806) According to a survey commissioned by the _[Blick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blick "Blick")_ newspaper on 10–15 November, 72% of Swiss respondents believed Israel had a right to defend itself and reply militarily in Gaza while 67% felt Switzerland should temporarily suspend financial aid to the Palestinian occupied territories. At the same time, 58% said Switzerland's approval of the UN resolution for a ceasefire was "fair" or "quite fair".[\[807\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-807) A survey conducted by the [Levada Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levada_Center "Levada Center") from 19 to 25 October 2023 found that 66% of Russian respondents expressed a neutral position on the conflict, 21% sympathized with the Palestinians, and 6% sympathized with Israel. 45% of respondents blamed the conflict's escalation on the United States and [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") (a view promoted by Russian state-controlled media and President [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin")), while 12% blamed Israel and 8% blamed Hamas.[\[808\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-808)[\[809\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-809) A survey conducted by the [Kyiv International Institute of Sociology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv_International_Institute_of_Sociology "Kyiv International Institute of Sociology") from 29 that 8% had participated in a protest for either side.[\[834\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-834) ### Opinions of Generation Z in the Western world The views espoused by members of [Generation Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_Z "Generation Z") in the Western world in response to the war gained the attention of researchers and political analysts, as there is a [generational divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_gap "Generation gap") between Generation Z and older generations on topics such as the [Israeli–Palestinian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict "Israeli–Palestinian conflict"), [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas"), and the [American government's support for Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_support_for_Israel_in_the_Gaza_war "United States support for Israel in the Gaza war").[\[835\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:03-835)[\[836\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-836) Notably, members of Generation Z were more likely to support Palestine and to oppose Israel than any other generation.[\[822\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-brookings.edu-822) According to an October 2023 NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist National poll which surveyed 1,313 U.S. adults, 48% of [Millennials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials") and Generation Z said that the U.S. government should publicly voice support for Israel, compared to 63% of [Generation X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_X "Generation X"), 83% of [Baby boomers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_boomers "Baby boomers"), and 86% from the [Silent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Generation "Silent Generation") and [Greatest Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_Generation "Greatest Generation").[\[822\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-brookings.edu-822)[\[823\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-Montanaro-823) Between 13 and 14 December 2023, an online survey was conducted by [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") and [The Harris Poll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Harris_Poll "The Harris Poll") among 2,034 Americans from all age groups. While the survey assessed a range of political issues, there were several questions about the Gaza war. While the Harvard-Harris poll found that 73% of those aged 18–24 believed that the [7 October attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hamas-led_attack_on_Israel "2023 Hamas-led attack on Israel") was a terrorist attack and 66% of those aged 18–24 believed that the 7 October attack was genocidal in nature, 60% of those polled aged 18–24 believed that the 7 October 2023 attack was justified by Palestinian grievances, with smaller subsets of 50% stating that they sided with Hamas and 51% favoring a [one-state solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-state_solution "One-state solution") where Israel would be ended and the land given completely to Hamas and the Palestinians. Furthermore, 67% of Generation Z respondents considered Jews to be oppressors, yet 69% of Generation Z respondents also stated that Israel has a right to exist.[\[835\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:03-835) Another poll in December 2023 was conducted by More in Common which surveyed various age groups, including Generation Z When members of Generation Z were asked whether they considered Hamas to be a terrorist organisation, Generation Z respondents were the most likely to consider Hamas to be freedom fighters and the least likely to consider Hamas a terrorist organisation.[\[837\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:17-837) Some research has credited the stance of Western countries' members of Generation Z to [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") and social media trends on the platform, with [_Axios_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axios_(website) "Axios (website)") noting that the platform has a large amount of Palestinian content on the website. The site found that 87% of TikTok users who view #StandwithPalestine posts are under the age of 35. In comparison, only 66% of TikTok users who view #StandwithIsrael posts are under the age of 35.[\[838\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:22-838) A trend was observed of Generation Z TikTok users sharing their [conversion to Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Islam "Conversion to Islam") following the Israel-Hamas war.[\[839\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-839) Lorenzo Vidino, director of the Programme on Extremism at [George Washington University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_University "George Washington University") has attributed this trend to a desire among Generation Z to rebel against Western values. Vidino stated: "At this point, what's more rebellious, what's more [anti-Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Western_sentiment "Anti-Western sentiment") and [anti-capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-capitalism "Anti-capitalism") and [anti-establishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-establishment "Anti-establishment"), than a conversion to Islam?"[\[840\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-:42-840) ## Analysis Hugh Lovatt, a senior policy fellow with the Middle East and North Africa Programme at the [European Council on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council_on_Foreign_Relations "European Council on Foreign Relations"), analysed in January 2024, that the strong diplomatic and military support from much of the [Western world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_world "Western world") (including US, UK, Germany) to Israel is "at odds with the attitudes of Western publics which continue to shift away from Israel". He said that during the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), Israel sided with the West against the Arab countries supported by the Soviets, and Western leaders generally see Israel "as a fellow member of the [liberal democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_democracy "Liberal democracy") club", which partially "explains the continued strong Western support for Israel – which has now largely become reflexive".[\[841\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-Busari-2024-841) According to [Andrew Stroehlein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Stroehlein "Andrew Stroehlein"), writing for [Human Rights Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Rights_Watch "Human Rights Watch") in October 2024, most countries of the world have supported their own side of the conflict, without caring for [human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights "Human rights").[\[842\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_Gaza_war#cite_note-842) ## See also -
